thread.title: Midday Update: Dow Rallies as Bargain-Hunting Boosts Financial, Technology Sectors

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: Dow Rallies as Bargain-Hunting Boosts Financial, Technology Sectors
text:
Shutterstock photo Stocks extended last week's rally as investors capitalized on buying opportunities in the financial and technology sectors, as well as by plans for President Trump to spend $200 billion on infrastructure.
Led by outsized gains in component shares Apple ( AAPL ), Boeing ( BA ) and Cisco ( CSCO ), the Dow Jones Industrial Average is more than 400 points higher, outpacing significant gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite. All three have climbed back over their respective 100-day moving averages.
Wall Street's tolerance for risk was undiminished by persistently higher Treasury yields with the 10-year note inching above 2.85% in reaction to increased government spending in President Donald Trump's budget. Despite $1.7 trillion in cuts to mandatory spending, the budget will cause the deficit to swell to more than $1 trillion, putting additional pressure on prices for Treasury securities, but leaving stocks unscathed.
The details of the budget compensated for Wall Street's dearth of economic data or quarterly results as investors brace for a flood of data in the second half of the week that includes inflation indicators, industrial production and earnings from Under Armour ( UA ) CBS ( CBS ) and Pepsico (PEP).
Europe's major market were all sharply higher Monday in tandem with the US with the UK's FTSE-100 staging an impressive comeback from Friday's 14-month low
Crude oil was up $1.00 to $60.20 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.03 to $2.56 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $10.30 to $1,326.00 an ounce, while silver was up $0.35 to $16.49 an ounce. Copper was up $0.04 to $3.07 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 0.76% to $11.95 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 1.18% to $21.77. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 2.46% to 21.84 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.68% to $125.62. The iShares Silver Trust was up 1.40% to $15.60.
